title: ML-driven criticality scoring for admission control + partial-response graceful degradation
creator: Alex Chen
description: Introduce an ML-driven request criticality scorer at the API edge to inform admission control and priority queue placement, enabling more surgical load shedding and structured partial-response strategies. The scorer is a lightweight model (logistic or small transformer) that predicts expected user impact and downstream cost of a request using request metadata and prompt signals. The admission controller uses the score plus tenant SLA contract and current capacity signals to decide: accept to fastlane, accept to slow-path, accept with partial response (trim/summarize), or reject. This ticket covers model spec, inference pathway, policy rules, observability, rollout and fallback (circuit breaker) integration.
acceptance_criteria: Edge scorer prototype returns a score for 100% of requests within 1ms P99 under normal load in the staging region
Admission controller accepts+routes requests according to score thresholds configured per-tenant
Partial-response generator produces syntactically valid, quality-check-passing outputs for 95% of sampled requests when invoked as graceful degradation
End-to-end SLO degradation during an induced overload test matches the expected trade-off curve (latency SLO preserved for P95 fastlane traffic; overall error rate within agreed contract)
Instrumentation emits score histograms, route decisions, and per-tenant cost delta metrics to Console dashboards
design_decisions: Use a compact feature set (tenant tier, route, prompt length, user-declared urgency hint, recent failure rate, model type) to keep scorer inference cheap
Run scorer synchronously in the edge proxy process for deterministic admission, with a CPU-bound path and small warm pool to meet low-latency constraints
Decision policy is policy-as-data: thresholds per-tenant are stored in ConfigService and hot-reloadable; default fallback policy is conservative (favor availability)
Partial response modes: truncation + suffix marker, abstractive summarization with model-constrained tokens, and structured 'status-only' responses for telemetry endpoints
Build feedback loop: log accepted/degraded/rejected cases, human-labeled impact samples and integrate into periodic scorer re-training cadence
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Canary (staging): deploy scorer binary and admission hook in staging region behind feature flag; run scoring-only mode (no routing changes) for 72h to validate distributions

Phase 1 - Hairline (small production subset): enable routing for 5% of traffic for non-enterprise tenants with safe thresholds; enable partial-response for low-risk routes only; monitor error budgets and quality metrics
Phase 2 - Regional expansion: progressively enable for additional regions with region-specific thresholds; activate slow-path autoscaling for slow-path pools
Phase 3 - Tenant opt-in and enterprise contracts: provide per-tenant policy UI and opt-out flags; for enterprise tenants use audit-log mode before any automatic degradation
Rollback: global feature toggle and immediate switch to score-pass-through mode; circuit breaker will enforce hard reject on sudden downstream failures
dependencies: ENG-517333 (stable-headroom-policy-layered-admission) - affinity to combine headroom with scoring
infra-proxy-team - edge proxy change for synchronous scorer hook
console-obs-team - dashboard panels and alerting for new metrics
privacy-team - review of logged features for PII and telemetry retention policy
notes: We purposely restrict model features to avoid sending user content to external services; all scoring runs on candidate edge binary approved for private deployments
Partial-response generator will reuse existing summarize-light model family; where summarization is not available we fall back to deterministic truncation with marker
We will add a soft-override header X-Force-Fastlane for internal test runs and partner debug sessions
